A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MCFlow research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–I are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original MCFlow experiments on crystal structure prediction, de novo generation, and atom type generation, together with ablations and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original MCFlow results and adds LeMat-GenBench evaluations, atom-substitution experiments, computational measurements, and further controlled comparisons.

M1.justification: V2 adds a limited inference adaptation for atom substitution: each atom-generation step overwrites known sites with their given types while sampling masked sites (Section 4.3). The core architecture, flow objectives, ordering, augmentation, and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged. Newly specified positional embeddings and prior parameters are implementation disclosures.

E1.justification: MP-20, MPTS-52, and the original three tasks remain. V2 introduces LeMat-Bulk as an evaluation reference and tests partially conditioned atom substitution on four MP-20 test crystals, fixing known species while generating masked species. These extend coverage within the existing inorganic-crystal domain.

E2.justification: The main DNG comparison adds MatterGen, PLaID++, standalone WyFormer variants, Crystal-GFN, CrystalFormer, DiffCSP, and LLaMat2/3-CIF; CDVAE, FlowMM, FlowLLM, OMatG, SGEquiDiff, and SGFM leave that table. FlowMM is also added to the ATG comparison in Table 3, and Table H.8 evaluates DNG-trained DiffCSP and FlowMM adapted to CSP.

E3.justification: The main DNG evaluation changes from 10,000 samples with CHGNet-based evaluation for MCFlow to 2,500 samples evaluated using three MLIPs and LeMat-Bulk hulls, with separate pre-relaxation conditions. Validity and matching rules change, percentages use all submitted structures, and metastability excludes stable structures. New protocols include METRe/cRMSE on original and polymorph-aware splits, filtered/unfiltered CSP, and 100 substitution samples per parent crystal.

E4.justification: V2 adds substantial tests of the central design choices: electronegativity versus atomic-number ordering and unrestricted permutation (H.4), CSP-only versus unified training (H.7), and coupled versus decoupled time axes (H.8). It also adds computational-cost analysis, evaluation-method sensitivity checks, and substitution case studies. The earlier guidance, permutation-space, scaling, and cumulative component analyses remain.

E5.justification: Table 2 newly reports means with standard deviations for formation energy, hull energy, and relaxation RMSD. Its caption specifies variation across 2,500 generated structures, averaged over three MLIPs. This adds distributional dispersion reporting, but does not establish repeated training runs or uncertainty across training seeds.

E6.justification: The main DNG results are replaced under different evaluation conditions, and multiple new result tables are added. Table 1 revises baseline scores: OMatG's MP-20 match rate changes from 61.88 to 63.75, with v2 specifying LinearODE, and CrystalFlow's single-sample MPTS-52 match rate changes from 22.71 to 21.00. Original MCFlow CSP and ATG entries largely remain unchanged; the new DNG numbers are not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The substantive flow equations, symmetry definitions, and mathematical development in Section 3 and Appendices A–B are retained. V2 clarifies notation and endpoint behavior. Its new cRMSE equation documents an adopted evaluation metric rather than introducing new theoretical reasoning or a proof.

C1.justification: The central claims of unified generation through independent modality times and symmetry-aware ordering remain. V2 adds atom substitution through fixed known sites as an explicit introduction contribution. This extends the claimed capability without redefining the paper's central contribution.

C2.justification: V1's larger-unit-cell limitation is replaced by explicit exclusions of amorphous/disordered systems and a stability–novelty trade-off. V2 also adds explanations involving cation–anion ordering, transformer computational efficiency, and scaling. It interprets the new training controls as evidence against destructive task interference and for the importance of decoupled time axes.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies fixed sinusoidal positional embeddings, lattice-length normalization by N^(1/3), and dataset-specific LogNormal parameters (Section 3.1; Table F.2). Table H.1 adds measured training and inference times with hardware and batch sizes. These improve documentation; the PDFs do not establish changes to the original implementation from these disclosures.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands to language-model and text-guided generation, hybrid pipelines, periodic Bayesian flows, Crystal-GFN, and Zatom-1, while removing several older generative-model citations. V2 also adds the LeMat and METRe evaluation foundations and claims structure-conditioned ATG was previously unstudied as a standalone generative task. These changes exceed bibliographic metadata updates.

P1.justification: V2 tightens the abstract, consolidates contribution bullets, clarifies method explanations, revises experimental discussion, and reorganizes Appendix H around tables. It adds a conflict-of-interest disclosure and updates publication information. The overall section sequence and most methodological and background prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Table 2 is extensively redesigned with new metric columns and pre-relaxation groups. V2 adds the substitution table and six Appendix H tables, relocates existing displays, and consolidates Algorithms 2–3 onto one page. Existing template-CSP and MPTS-52 tables survive as H.3/H.6. Captions are revised, and the retained scaling plot loses its correlation-coefficient annotations.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central method. Table 2 and Appendix G replace heterogeneous DNG comparisons with a documented common protocol and model-consistent hulls. Tables H.4, H.7, and H.8 directly test ordering, unified training, and time decoupling, addressing important gaps in v1's support. Polymorph/filtering checks and explicit stability–novelty limitations further improve credibility. The changed DNG protocol prevents direct score comparisons, and sample dispersion does not quantify training variability, but these limits do not outweigh the stronger evaluation.
